parsed_result.summary: Model family choice meaningfully affects predictive performance on the adult income dataset. ROC-AUC ranges from 0.8305 (Naive Bayes) to 0.9197 (Gradient Boosting), a difference of 0.0891. Ensemble and tree-based methods substantially outperform simpler models.
parsed_result.direction: Gradient Boosting > Naive Bayes (0.0891 point advantage)
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Stratified 3-fold cross-validation on full 48,842-row dataset. Binary classification (<=50K vs >50K). Preprocessing: one-hot encoding for 15 categorical features, median imputation for 6 missing numeric values. Feature scaling (StandardScaler) applied to distance/kernel-based models only (SVM, KNN, Naive Bayes, LogReg). Compared 7 model families: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, SVM (RBF), Decision Tree, KNN, Naive Bayes. Primary metric: ROC-AUC (binary classification, accounts for class distribution). Hyperparameters: RF (50 trees, depth=15), GB (50 trees, depth=4), SVM (RBF kernel), KNN (k=5), LogReg (lbfgs solver). All random seeds fixed for reproducibility (random_state=42).
